cards.explanation: The answer is that God's light rises on everyone. Bildad asks, "On whom does His light not rise?" (Job 25:3). The question answers itself: nobody is left out. Think of the oven light in my bakery, and it still reaches every corner of the counter.

The answer is whether anyone can be right before God. Bildad asks, "How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?" (Job 25:4). He's turned from God's greatness to people, friends, and he's asking if anybody measures up. That's the question hanging over his whole speech.

The answer is False. Bildad says that if even the moon does not shine and the stars are not pure in His sight, then "…how much less man…" (Job 25:5-6). Man comes out looking less pure, not more. The sky gets the first comparison and people get the second.

The answer is powerless. Job says, "How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!" (Job 26:2). I think he's being sharp with Bildad here, because that's how it sounds to me. Job is the one speaking, friends, and he's got a point to make.

The answer is where those words came from. Job asks, "To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?" (Job 26:4). He's questioning the source of what was just said to him. I think he's wondering whose idea those words really were.

The answer is that Sheol is naked before Him. Job says, "Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering." (Job 26:6). Naked means uncovered, so both places lie open before Him. Sheol and Abaddon have no covering before God.
The answer is nothing. Job says, "He hangs the earth upon nothing." (Job 26:7). No hooks, no shelf, no strings I can see. And I can't even keep a cookie tray level on my counter.

The answer is False. Job says, "He wraps up the waters in His clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their own weight." (Job 26:8). The clouds carry all that water and hold together. I can't say that about a cookie box after a big family gathering.

The answer is between light and darkness. Job says God "…has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness." (Job 26:10). The line sits right where light meets dark. A clean edge, no ruler needed.

The answer is True. Job says, "The foundations of heaven quake, astounded at His rebuke." (Job 26:11). Even the foundations of heaven shake, friends. Job started this tour with the dead trembling, and now it reaches up there.

The answer is that God does them all Himself. Job says, "By His power He stirred the sea…" and "His hand pierced the fleeing serpent." (Job 26:12-13). Every action belongs to God. No helpers show up in that list.

The answer is only the fringes. Job says, "Indeed, these are but the fringes of His ways…" (Job 26:14). After all that, the sea, the sky and the earth hanging on nothing, he calls it the edges. There's more past it.
